headline: Smotrich threatens Egypt over Sinai, calls for annexing southern Lebanon to Beirut line, and Gaza depopulation as 'final solution'
dek: Smotrich: (1) EGYPT — does not trust Sisi's assurances (Sisi last week: no territorial ambitions, 1979 treaty stands); warns Egypt could lose the Sinai if it attacks Israel: 'If they understand that the next time they attack, there will be no Sinai, that is the guarantee.' (2) LEBANON — Israel…
sources: Bezalel Smotrich, Israeli Finance Minister / Religious Zionism leader, in interview with Israeli platform 'Ali Express'
fault_line: Election rhetoric or actual doctrine? A sitting minister maps three annexations in one interview — is the government listening, or is this campaign theater eight days out?

sections.what_happened: Smotrich: (1) EGYPT — does not trust Sisi's assurances (Sisi last week: no territorial ambitions, 1979 treaty stands); warns Egypt could lose the Sinai if it attacks Israel: 'If they understand that the next time they attack, there will be no Sinai, that is the guarantee.' (2) LEBANON — Israel should annex occupied southern Lebanon 'at least up to the lines where we are positioned today' (earlier: 8-12 km); 'if Hezbollah attacks again, then all the way to Beirut. And if it attacks again, then even beyond that.' Claims northern border 'not defensible'. (3) GAZA — wants Gaza kept small, overcrowded, in ruins to push Palestinians out; prefers to call depopulation 'final solution and readjustment for the refugee problem' internationally. (4) Also raised Türkiye threat concerns (Erdoğan successor, navy). Said he told/advises Trump that Israel needs 'defensible borders'. Context: Oct 27 Israeli elections; interview described as election-timed by Egyptian media observers. Egyptian MP Mustafa Bakri and TV host Ahmed Moussa answered with threats ('all 120 million Egyptians would die defending Egypt').
sections.what_verified: Anadolu (Oct 20), Eastora News (Oct 20, full quotes), Demócrata (Oct 20), Al Mayadeen (60% of Gaza annexation figure), JFeed (JPost relay of Egyptian backlash). Consistent quotes across outlets.
sections.what_disputed: Smotrich is Finance Minister, NOT Defense Minister — his remarks are coalition-hardliner rhetoric, not confirmed government policy. The Sinai threat is CONDITIONAL ('if they attack'); earlier Oct 5 version drew same Egyptian backlash. Eastora's 'Trump' reference and Demócrata's 'former US president' line reflect outlet slant, not Smotrich's title — do not use.
sections.why_matters: Three fronts in one interview: Sinai threat to Egypt, Beirut-line annexation, and Gaza depopulation branded a 'final solution.' Put the exact quotes on screen with named sources, then the Egyptian backlash. TOTW stance: treat the annexation doctrine as the story's core (not a gaffe); label him as coalition hardliner, not cabinet policy — and note the Oct 27 election timing.
